# 0057: Each harness declares a model catalogue, with a hand-curated family tier frozen at release

Status: accepted, 2026-10-06.
Where the catalogue lives is superseded by [0059](0059-the-model-catalogue-is-one-config-file-beside-the-prices.md): one config file, not a list on each harness class.
The tier, line and release-date decisions stand.
Refines:

- [0034](0034-a-harness-is-a-class-and-the-registry-is-the-only-dispatch.md) (a harness is a class) with a fifth question asked of a harness
- [0007](0007-unpriced-model-aborts-before-spend.md) (an unpriced model aborts before spend) with an uncatalogued model aborting the same way

Additive:

- `result.json` gains `line`, `family_tier` and `released`
- `history.json` gains the same three keys
- `report/index.json` gains the same three keys

## Context

A model was a bare string.
It appeared in the plugin-default matrix and in the dated price records, and nowhere said what kind of model it was.
Comparing the treatment sweeps across eight models from two providers needed exactly that.
Which models are the small ones on each side? Which are the flagships?

Two candidate signals were researched and rejected as the bucket.
Price drifts: GPT-6 Luna matches Sonnet 5 on a capability index at a twentieth of the price.
A continuous capability index such as Epoch's ECI does not bucket, and drifts across generations.
Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5.6 Luna both fill the smallest role in their lineups, yet sit three ECI tiers apart.

No comparator publishes a cross-provider size class or generation field either.
The one grouping field they all share is the release date.

## Decision

**Each harness class declares its `models`, beside its effort ladder.** One `ModelSpec` per supported model holds four curated facts: `id`, `line`, `family_tier` and `released`.
A provider's differences live on its class (ADR 0034), so there is no table of models keyed by harness name.
`model/registry.py` gathers them into a `Catalogue`, the fifth lookup it answers for the domain.

**`line` is the provider's own product line.** It is the word Anthropic's Models API publishes and models.dev calls `family`: haiku, sonnet, opus, fable, luna, terra, sol, astra.

**`family_tier` is a hand-curated integer for the model's role in its lineup, 1 the smallest.** It is a number because a name is reassigned when a lineup changes, while a number keeps sliding.
It is a role and never a price, so GPT-6 Sol is tier 3 beside Opus although its rates sit with tier-2 models.
It is frozen at release: a model keeps the tier it shipped with.
A lineup that later gains or loses a line renumbers only the models that follow.

**`released` is the release date, and no generation format is decided.** A cohort derived from it, such as a quarter, was considered and deferred.

**A project may add or correct a model before a plugin release.** An `xharness_models` ini line in the shape of `xharness_prices` does it, and the project's line wins.

**A matrix entry naming an uncatalogued model stops collection, before spend.** The refusal names the `xharness_models` line that would add it, the same way an unpriced model is refused (ADR 0007).

**The three facts are stored on every record.** The derivation pipeline copies `line`, `family_tier` and `released` from the catalogue.
An archived run then states what it was without the catalogue that produced it.
A replay carries stored values forward and looks up older captures, which is the same answer because a tier is frozen.

## Consequences

The plugin default matrix is no longer a hand-kept list: it is derived from the catalogue, filtered by cost (ADR 0058).
The price curator now checks that every catalogued model is priced, not only the default matrix.
A test checks that every bundled model is priced today and that no harness skips a tier.

The characterization goldens gain the three keys with real values, `opus` and `sol` at tier 3, which is the intended behaviour change.

Gated models, such as the Mythos line and `gpt-5.6-cyber`, are not catalogued.
Neither are retired ones, and older captures of them still replay with the three keys left null.

## Lens

A cross-provider comparison needs a bucket that survives a lineup change.
Names get reassigned when a provider retires a line or adds one above the top.
Numbers can keep sliding, and a number frozen at release keeps history comparable.
Curate the few facts a measurement cannot supply, and compute everything else.
